abstract: Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey, biweekly cycle 202621, published October 22, 2026. Question 7 asks whether a business used AI - relabelled in this vintage as 'Super Intelligence or SI (formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI)' - in any of its business functions in the last two weeks; Question 24 asks whether it expects to within six months. This is the highest-frequency firm-side AI adoption measure in the US and the series jobsdata.ai plots on ai-adoption-rate. Values are dated to reference-period end, which for BTOS falls six to seven weeks before publication.
keyFindings: National AI use was 24.6 percent of firms (SE 0.27 percent) for the two weeks ending 2026-10-04, up 0.8 points from 23.8 percent for the cycle ending 2026-09-20 - the series resumes rising after one flat cycle and 24.6 percent is its highest reading.

The six-month expectation of AI use (Q24) was 28.6 percent (SE 0.21 percent), up 0.9 points from 27.7 percent, so expected use rose about as fast as current use and the gap between the two held near 4.0 points.
The standard error narrowed back from 0.41 to 0.27 percent, so this estimate is more precise than the flat cycle before it and the 0.8-point rise sits outside the sampling error of either cycle.
Current use has risen 3.1 points since the cycle ending 2026-07-12 (21.5 percent), an average of about 0.45 points per cycle across seven cycles.

This vintage of National.xlsx relabels the Q7 and Q24 wording from 'Artificial Intelligence (AI)' to 'Super Intelligence or SI (formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI)' across every cycle in the workbook, with new examples ('SI-powered data analysis; generative SI for marketing, product design, or coding; virtual SI agents for customer service; SI-powered forecasting or pricing; SI-driven computer vision for quality control'). Estimates for cycles 202614 through 202620 are unchanged from the prior vintage, so this is a terminology relabel in the published instrument rather than a re-survey or a change of construct.
methodology: Biweekly establishment survey across a large national sample of about 1.2 million US businesses, published as an experimental data product. Each estimate is collected over a two-week window covering a two-week reference period ending six to seven weeks before publication; cycle 202621 was collected 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-18 for the reference period 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-04. The November 2025 rewording from AI use 'in producing goods or services' to 'in any business function', and the October 2026 relabelling of AI as SI, are both same-construct instrument changes, and Census publishes one continuous series.
qualifiers: A firm-level adoption share, not a measure of how much work AI performs. It counts any use in the prior two weeks, so it sets a low bar per firm and says nothing about intensity - other surveys find that adopters apply AI to a minority of tasks. Not directly comparable to posting-based measures or to payment-based measures such as the Ramp AI Index, which read far higher on narrower or self-selected footprints. The biannual AI Supplement, now linked as a 'Questionnaire with SI Supplement', is a separate instrument with an 11-week reference window and should not be treated as the latest point in this series. The AI questions appear in every cycle; the press releases are boilerplate and never mention AI, so the National.xlsx workbook is the only reliable read.
